source.title: SLAM: Structural Linguistic Activation Marking for Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses Gemma Scope SAEs for structural feature mining and watermark steering, but does not test whether larger SAE dictionaries split smaller-dictionary features or whether their inputs partition.
record.gate_note: No results compare SAE dictionary sizes or match features across dictionaries. The reported feature counts and k-ablation concern structural directions used for watermarking, not feature splitting; only the adjacent representation-distribution statements are recorded below.
record.test_reason: The paper is a watermarking method. It uses Gemma Scope 16k SAEs as a tool to mine and steer syntactic directions. It never varies dictionary size, matches features across dictionaries, examines parent/child firing, or compares SAE objectives. Towards Monosemanticity is cited only as background on SAEs, not for feature splitting. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that steering SAE-derived structural (syntactic) directions gives a watermark with 100% TPR and small quality cost on Gemma-2 2B/9B. Composite k=10 SVD directions are needed at 9B because structural representations are distributed. The scheme is robust to word-level edits but vulnerable to syntax-restructuring paraphrase. The authors draw no conclusion about feature splitting.
record.recipe_differences: Uses public Gemma Scope SAEs to mine and steer structural directions for watermarking; it does not train or compare SAEs at increasing dictionary sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed SAE width (16k), structural concepts are said to be carried by a handful of features in Gemma-2 2B but spread over 5–15 weak features in 9B. Single-direction (k=1) steering caps at 90% TPR on 9B versus 100% on 2B (Table 7, Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed SAE width, syntactic concepts are spread across more SAE latents in larger models, so composite multi-latent directions are needed to capture them.

record.problems: No direct evidence about feature splitting: the study holds SAE width at 16k and does not track corresponding features across dictionaries. Code and feature banks are described as planned for release upon publication.
record.rows_left_out: Watermark detection, quality, robustness, and k-by-steering-strength results were left out because they evaluate the watermarking method rather than dictionary-size feature splitting.

untested.parts: Entire version: no dictionary-size sweep, no cross-dictionary feature matching, no input-coverage test.
Entire version: two Gemma-2 sizes are used, but at one SAE width and with no splitting analysis.
Entire version: no nested families or geometric parent–child analysis.
Entire version: no absorption or parent/child firing analysis, and no size or sparsity sweep.
Entire version: no decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents.
Entire version: no comparison of training objectives and no Matryoshka SAEs.

record.verdict_notes: A watermarking application paper with no bearing on feature-splitting versions. The fits_no_version item is a model-size effect at constant SAE width, not dictionary-size splitting, and rests mainly on an author assertion plus an indirect k-ablation.

versions.untested_parts: Entire version: no dictionary-size sweep, cross-dictionary feature matching, or input-partition test.
Entire version: using models of two sizes does not test the claimed splitting pattern across dictionary sizes or SAE releases.
Entire version: no nested feature families or geometric closeness between parent and child features are measured.
Entire version: parent-child firing overlap and effects of SAE size or sparsity are not tested.
Entire version: no decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents or assessment of novel latents.
Entire version: no comparison of SAE training objectives, correlated-input effects, or Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 2B
rows.operation_detail: Authors describe how many SAE features co-activate for structural concepts.
rows.measure: Number of co-activating SAE features per concept
rows.note: This describes feature distribution within the SAE, not a feature split across dictionary sizes.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. This is a qualitative author statement ('a handful' of co-activating features) at a single SAE width (16k) on Gemma-2 2B. It has no dictionary-size comparison and no baseline, so it cannot bear on splitting.

rows.subject: Gemma-2 9B
rows.operation_detail: Authors describe how many SAE features represent structural concepts.
rows.measure: Number of weakly discriminative SAE features per concept
rows.note: Authors say single-feature mining discards signal and k>1 is necessary at this scale; this is not a cross-dictionary splitting test.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. The '5–15 weakly-discriminative features' figure for 9B is asserted in §3.3 without a reported measurement. It is indirectly consistent with Table 7/Fig. 4, where k=1 caps at 90% TPR on 9B. Width is held at 16k while model width changes, so this is not a dictionary-size test. The numbers_found field '1/1' is uninformative.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
